subject.gist: Sara and Jérémie turned a retired cargo barge into a home, buying plants before furniture and finding relief from stress watching the water.

story.text: Jérémie dreams of living beside the water; Sara takes two years to warm to the idea of a houseboat. Together they turn a retired cargo barge into Panjab, a home full of light and plants, which they buy before the furniture. Glass stairs carry daylight down into rooms beside the water, and a table for twelve finally gives them space to welcome family and friends. The long conversion tests Sara's patience, but the result feels worth it. Watching the river lets the day's stress fall away. They like being home so much that going out now takes an effort, even with Paris so close.

coverage.title: Seine moorings and bank approach
coverage.visible: Opening channel ident, aerial river views, neighboring moored boats and Sara walking with the interviewer on the leafy bank.
coverage.gaps: No exact municipality, berth boundary or ownership of the bank is established.

coverage.title: Gangway and Panjab entrance
coverage.visible: Continuous walk across the railed gangway and circular metal gate to Panjab’s planted deck and glazed upper room.
coverage.gaps: No mooring contract or structural specifications are shown.

coverage.title: Glazed upper living room
coverage.visible: Glass floor panel, rooflights, tall windows, potted plants, suspended fireplace, dining zone and unguarded narrow waterside ledge.
coverage.gaps: No glazing specification, fireplace fuel or glass floor loading is established.

coverage.title: River outlook and wildlife
coverage.visible: Aerials and upper-room interview with Sara and Jérémie, intercut with swan, fish, ducks and a brown waterside rodent.
coverage.gaps: Wildlife species and the claimed stress reduction are not independently established.

coverage.title: Planted decks and plant care
coverage.visible: Pots, climbing vegetation, gangway, green dinghy and upper lounge frame the discussion of caring for plants.
coverage.gaps: No species inventory, irrigation system or food yield is demonstrated.

coverage.title: Glass stairs and lower lounge
coverage.visible: Continuous descent over transparent treads beside plants into the lounge with blue sofa and round/elongated windows near river level.
coverage.gaps: No waterproofing or stair engineering detail is exposed.

coverage.title: Former engine room and laundry
coverage.visible: Heavy white original door opens into storage with a washing machine, worktop and round window.
coverage.gaps: Engine removal itself is not filmed; electrical and plumbing routes are not shown.

coverage.title: Archive: retired cargo hull

coverage.gaps: Exact archive date and shipyard location are absent.

coverage.title: Archive photographs and purchase account

coverage.gaps: Phone images do not establish a complete work sequence or total conversion cost.

coverage.title: Archive: hull conversion work
coverage.visible: Inserted construction footage shows bare steel ribs, new round and elongated window openings, overhead framework and workers.
coverage.gaps: No wall build-up, engineering calculations or inspections are documented.

coverage.title: Archive: signs, repainting and launch
coverage.visible: Phone photographs show PANJAB lettering, worksite sign, repainted hull, launching and assistance from another boat.
coverage.gaps: No precise launch date, lettering provenance or worksite address is given.

coverage.title: River connection and finished exterior
coverage.visible: Archive towing images give way to current deck interview and aerials of the completed houseboat; Jérémie’s personal history is subtitled.
coverage.gaps: Current images are not evidence of his earlier homelessness or childhood home.

coverage.title: Outdoor hospitality and guests

coverage.gaps: The guest is not named and no occupancy schedule is established.
